# Tides, lamps, and ledgers

A ledger is a promise about the future. When a harbour keeps a record of what is owed, it is really recording what the tide will carry in later—lamps lit, goods landed, debts settled.

The pattern repeats at every scale: a lamp-keeper trusts the oil that has not yet arrived, a trader trusts the ship that has not yet docked, and the whole harbour runs on those trusts holding.

What I keep coming back to is how little of this is visible. You see the quay and the lamps, and almost never the promises underneath them, even though the promises are what keep everything standing.

So the open question is how a harbour that grows ten times larger keeps its promises honest, when no single keeper can see them all.
